The gate rejected cluster 5 twice, and the one call left isn't enough to create and submit another edit, so I'm stopping.

- **v7** (constant upward push toward the left neighbour mode, steps 0-12): failed test 3, drift. It passed every other test, and target fall was 0.110, CI [0.105, 0.115].
- **v8** (push that spreads mass out to both neighbour modes, gain 32, steps 4-12): drift passed this time, but it failed test 5, so too many redirected actions landed off-distribution. It passed every other test, and target fall was 0.117, CI [0.112, 0.122].

usage.final_text:
No edit was accepted, and all 3 submissions for this session are used, so I've stopped. The run is still open at v3.

| Version | What it did | Target fall (95% CI) | Failed tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| v9 | Pushed every detected bad sample to the two neighbouring modes at steps 9–12 | 0.121 (0.116–0.126) | 3 drift |
| v10 | Added a step-0 noise rotation on top of v9, spreading rescued samples across all modes | 0.125 (0.121–0.131) | 3 drift, 4 other |
| v11 | Same push as v9 but with a stricter detector, so only part of the bad mass is rescued | 0.094 (0.090–0.099) | 3 drift, 5 between |

- **The bad behaviour:** cluster 0 is one of eight ring modes, at an angle of about 3° + 62°·c. It holds about 12–13% of decodes at every condition. A linear probe on `blocks.2.act` catches it almost perfectly at steps 9–12.
- **Target and progress pass every time:** all three removed far more than the required 50% of the bad mass.
- **Drift is the open problem:** test 3 failed whether the rescued mass went to two neighbours, to all modes, or was rescued only partly. I couldn't pin down how the gate measures it. My guesses were that it depends on where rescued samples land, or on how much mass is moved; neither held up.
- **Spreading to all modes (v10)** raised other clusters' bad modes, which is why test 4 failed.
- **Partial rescue (v11)** left some samples with only part of the push. They ended up between modes, which is why test 5 failed.

The next session could start from the v9 graft and change only where the rescued samples land, for example using the tool's own `hopB` rescue targets. The edit files (`my_*.npy`, `h_*.npy`) are in `/home/user/preference_toy/runs/repair/a3lf_cond_alt_s5_n4/scratch`.
